title: The Briefing
tagline: AI intelligence for Gauntlet AI — May 2, 2026

items.headline: GPT-5.5 Sets New SOTA on Reasoning Benchmarks
items.summary: OpenAI's latest flagship model GPT-5.5 achieves top-tier scores on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and ARC-AGI-2, outperforming competitors on reasoning tasks. However, it shows higher hallucination rates than some peers on knowledge recall benchmarks, particularly the AA-Omniscience Index which penalizes confident errors.

items.headline: Kimi K2.6 Leads Open-Weight Models in Agentic Capabilities
items.summary: Moonshot AI's updated Kimi model handles longer autonomous coding sessions and scales multi-agent orchestration. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Kimi K2.6 (54 points) leads open-weight models but trails GPT-5.5 (60 points) and Claude Opus 4.7 (57 points). On Arena.ai's Code Arena WebDev rankings, it places sixth among 67 models.

items.headline: Strategic Thinking Differs Between LLMs and Humans
items.summary: Researchers from UT Austin and Google found that LLMs like GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro model opponents more systematically than humans in rock-paper-scissors, tracking sequential patterns rather than just the opponent's last move. This demonstrates LLMs encode game strategies more thoroughly, revealing functional differences in decision-making algorithms.

items.headline: Big AI's Climate Commitments Under Strain
items.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft acknowledge that meeting AI demand is interfering with earlier climate pledges. While investing in renewables, they're building natural gas plants to meet rapid demand, with emissions rising significantly (54-60% increases since 2020). The tension between clean energy goals and scale-up needs is forcing companies toward fossil fuels in the near term.

items.headline: Data Centers Account for Growing Electricity Demand
items.summary: In 2024, data centers accounted for 1.5% of global electricity consumption and 4.4% in the U.S., projected to rise to 12% within years. Well-run data centers remain most efficient, but the sharp rise in AI demand is pushing companies toward further fossil fuel reliance despite earlier clean energy commitments.
